coverage.evidence: MathTemplateHelpers.cs:15-24 registers four groups: the expression row (MathExpressionHelpers.cs:16, exactly one argument at :20), the functions (MathFunctionHelpers.cs:17-22: sqrt, abs, floor, ceil take 1 number, pow takes 2, log takes 1 or 2), the operators (MathOperatorHelpers.cs:17-26, 2 numbers each via :34-39) and the aggregates (MathAggregateHelpers.cs:17-33, 1 to int.MaxValue numbers). The meter rows are in MeterBarHelpers.cs:19-28. That is 16 math rows and 4 meter rows, 20 in total, as the description says. A wrong argument count gives null in NumberHelperRow.cs:51-67.

NumberText.cs:22-26 rounds to 10 places half away from zero and formats with 0.########## in InvariantCulture, so 10/3 gives 3.3333333333 and 2.50*2 gives 5. Null makes the token print as written (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:45, :117-118). NumberMath.cs:26-28 returns null for a divisor of 0. NumberMath.cs:30-31 returns null for a negative square root. NumberMath.cs:33-36 returns null for a log of 0 or less and for a base of 0 or less or 1. NumberMath.cs:63-66 returns null for 0 to a negative power. NumberMath.cs:56-61 gives the median as the mean of the middle two for an even count. decimal.Truncate in MathOperatorHelpers.cs:21-25 gives -3 for -7|2, and C# % gives -1. An overflow is caught in NumberHelperGroup.cs:62-65, and FromDouble at NumberMath.cs:74-75 returns null for a non-finite or out-of-range double.

NumberHelperRow.cs:81-91 gives every row TemplateHelperContexts.StandardAndViewer, which is every value of the enum (TemplateHelperContexts.cs:25-26). The values are Command, EventResponse, Timer, Pipeline, Discord, Webhook and Viewer (TemplateHelperContext.cs:18-63). TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:131-132 filters helpers by context. Viewer text needs use_viewer_templates (ViewerTemplateCapabilities.cs:27, labeled Viewer Templates at FeatureService.cs:92-99). It also needs reward:input:template, which defaults to Subscriber (ActionDefinitionSeeder.cs:629-638).

ParsedArgument.cs:35-41 parses with AllowLeadingSign and AllowDecimalPoint in InvariantCulture, with no thousands separators and no exponent, after Trim (ParsedArgument.cs:24). So 2,5, 1,000 and 1e3 fail and the helper stays in braces through NumberHelperRow.cs:51-67. Inside an expression, MathExpression.cs:131-143 reads only digits and dots, and a leftover character fails AtEnd (MathExpression.cs:36).

MathExpression.cs:53-115 sets precedence from low to high: + and -, then * / %, then unary minus, then ^ binding to the right (ParsePower calls ParseUnary for the exponent at :113). So -2^2 gives -4, (-2)^2 gives 4 and 2^3^2 gives 512. Brackets are handled at :145-150. Function arguments are split on commas at :166-178. An unknown function or a wrong arity gives null (:180-191). The 200-character limit is MaxLength at :25 and :31. An unfinished expression gives null through ParsePrimary at :120-121. Inner tokens render before the outer helper runs (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:28-48), so a filled-in value counts toward the 200 characters, and {math:lots*2} fails at ParseCall (:159-160).

MeterBars.cs:17-18 sets the default width to 10 and the maximum to 50. MeterBars.cs:33-34 allows a width of 1 to 50 with digits only. MeterBars.cs:23-27 clamps to 0..100 and rounds the full marks half away from zero. MeterBarHelpers.cs:40-53 refuses exactly 3 arguments (full mark without empty) and prints the clamped percentage. :56-59 handles meter.plain with at most 2 arguments. :62-65 draws 5 hearts. :68-81 takes a whole star maximum from 1 to 20 (MaxStars at :33) and uses value/max*100 clamped. In viewer text, ViewerCountLimit.cs:31-45 cuts a whole-number width above the limit to the limit (MaxTextCount 20, IViewerTemplateResolver.cs:41; TemplateResolver.cs:121) before TryWidth runs.

reader_answers.evidence: The forms named match the registered rows and their argument counts (MathExpressionHelpers.cs:16-20, MathOperatorHelpers.cs:17-26, MathAggregateHelpers.cs:17-33, MeterBarHelpers.cs:19-28, :40-81). The nested progress example resolves inside out (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:28-48), and args.1 is the first word (ArgumentKeys.cs:18).

Every row is open to every template surface and to viewer text (NumberHelperRow.cs:81-91, TemplateHelperContexts.cs:25-26). Viewer text needs the use_viewer_templates feature, labeled Viewer Templates (FeatureService.cs:92-99), and the template permission, which defaults to Subscriber (ActionDefinitionSeeder.cs:629-638). The decimal dot rule is ParsedArgument.cs:35-41.

A null result prints as written (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:45, :117-118). Math rows return numbers through NumberText.Plain (NumberText.cs:22-26). meter, meter.plain and meter.hearts read a percentage, and meter.stars reads value and max (MeterBarHelpers.cs:40-81).

45/60*100 is exactly 75 in decimal. With the default width of 10 (MeterBars.cs:17), 7.5 rounds half away from zero to 8 (MeterBars.cs:25; NumberText.cs:32-33), giving 75%. 45/0 gives null (NumberMath.cs:26), so the inner token prints as written, and the outer meter then fails to parse it as a number and prints {meter:{math:45/0*100}} (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:117-118). A width of 0 or above 50 fails at MeterBars.cs:33-34. A single custom mark fails at MeterBarHelpers.cs:43. A percentage is clamped at MeterBars.cs:30.
